newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids remain mostly up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids remain mostly up.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat cash bids remained mostly higher on Friday as farm sales slowed down in the northern Plains and Pacific Northwest.
"There is no movement, it is at a complete standstill," an Oregon merchandiser said.

The focus was on winter seeding. Mild clear weather aided winter wheat seeding in Montana for the week ended October 6, allowing crop progress to catch up with averages, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.
Winter wheat was 65 percent planted against 32 percent a week ago, last year's 78 percent and the 69 percent average.

Dry weather also allowed winter wheat seeding and row crop harvesting to resume in South Dakota during the week ending Sunday, according to the weekly crop report from the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
South Dakota winter wheat was 72 percent seeded, against the five-year average of 94 percent. The crop was 48 percent emerged.
